evidence: The hunk passes horizon_manifest_memento_ref (a promptctl/memento sha) into horizon_goal_wording_file against this repo's object DB; cfbb498 replaces it with horizon_manifest_ref ... goal_wording, and the agent reports the memento sha dying with 'missing horizon/GOAL_PROMPT.md' as predicted.
guidance_note: When a rebase moves a component to another repository, grep every consumer of that component's recorded sha and check which repo each one resolves it in.

evidence: pin-instrument.sh's new horizon_provision_config_dir "$HORIZON_CONFIG_DIR" rm -rf's a fixed shared path with no serialization; the agent built a session-as-lock (horizon_live_run_config_dir) instead of a lock file, which was a defensible choice but covered only launched runs and spawned F25, F26, F27, F30, F32, F53 and F61.
guidance_note: Before naming a lock design, list every writer of each shared singleton (pin, run-loop, login, verify) and every window between invocation start and launch, and check the lock covers all of them.

evidence: diff -r does compare contents only, so an exec-bit loss would pass unseen; whether claude plugin install actually drops the bit is not shown in the packet, so the hazard is hypothetical but the check is cheap and matches the pin-time check.
guidance_note: When adding a pin-time invariant (finalize-session executable), add the same assertion to the verifier that checks the installed copy in the same commit.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 (memento sha used as a laws-repo commit); fixed in the same cfbb498 change.

Under set -u the trap's rm -f "$HORIZON_GOAL_FILE" fires on unset names when the script dies before line 145; cfbb498 moves mktemp above the trap so the unset state cannot exist, rather than initializing to empty strings.
guidance_note: When installing an EXIT trap that references globals, create those globals before the trap line.

evidence: login.sh reparsed claude auth status inline with 2>/dev/null and a bare json.load, diverging from horizon_assert_authenticated; cfbb498 makes horizon_auth_state the one reader and login.sh branches on its value.
guidance_note: When a script needs a check that lib.sh already implements as an assertion, factor the predicate out of the assertion first instead of rewriting it inline.

evidence: The sort key mixes aware _start values with datetime.max.replace(tzinfo=None), which raises TypeError; 5827d0c uses a UTC-aware fallback with a mutation-checked test.
guidance_note: When writing a sentinel for a sort key, construct it with the same type and timezone as the real values.

evidence: The docstring advertises a --mutate mode that main() never reads; the agent confirms the sweep was manual and removes the claim, which was one of the two options the reviewer offered.
guidance_note: Do not document a CLI flag in a docstring unless the same commit adds the code that parses it.

evidence: Third duplicate of F1; fixed in cfbb498.

The reviewer's claim depends on claude being a shebang wrapper; the agent reports `file` showing a Mach-O arm64 executable and `ps -eo comm=` printing claude for live sessions, and the code comment already records that the pane pid is claude. This is the agent's own stated probe, not something the packet shows directly.
The comment lists four gates including a custom-API-key prompt, but gates()/bypass() write no such key; the agent shrinks the comment to the three gates the code writes.
guidance_note: When a comment enumerates what a function handles, check each item against the function body before committing it.

evidence: Same duplicated auth parse as F6, including the 2>/dev/null divergence; same horizon_auth_state fix.
Fourth duplicate of F1; fixed in cfbb498.
The README edited one line to $HORIZON_CONFIG_DIR but kept the 'config/ under <run-dir>' bullet, which pin-instrument.sh no longer produces; cfbb498 removes it.
guidance_note: When moving an artifact's location, grep the README for every mention of the old path, not just the line next to the code change.

evidence: Under set -e the unguarded python pipeline exiting 3 or 4 kills the script before the case block, so its messages are unreachable (the agent confirmed this); the fix prints logged-in/logged-out instead of an exit-code protocol, which removes the problem rather than capturing rc.
guidance_note: Under set -e, never follow a command with `case "$?"`; return a value on stdout or capture the status in the same statement.

evidence: Duplicate of F7; fixed in 5827d0c.
`for pr in $(gh pr list ...)` swallows a failing listing; cfbb498 lists into variables first. But it fetched branches before the PR-closing loop, and that ordering produced F31.
guidance_note: When hoisting a lazily evaluated `for x in $(...)` into an eager variable, check whether anything between the old and new evaluation points mutates what the listing reads.

evidence: horizon_launch_session's unconditional kill-session reaps a live run; cfbb498 drops the kill and relies on the session-as-lock. Without the kill, nothing tore the session down after a run, which F29 then caught.
guidance_note: When removing a cleanup step that also served as teardown, add the teardown back at the owner's exit path in the same change.

evidence: The divergence only bites when HORIZON_CONFIG_DIR is overridden with a relative or symlinked path, since the default is absolute; deleting login.sh's canonicalization leaves one spelling, which is simpler than adding a second transform.
gh pr list defaults to 30 items and the branches API to 30 per page, so 'closes every open PR' did not hold; cfbb498 uses gh api --paginate with per_page=100 in shared helpers.
guidance_note: When a comment promises 'every' item from a remote API, paginate the listing in the same change.

evidence: horizon_bind_remote resets a shared GitHub repo with nothing serializing concurrent drivers; the cfbb498 fix only checked for a launched tmux session at startup, which left the setup window open (F26, F27) and put a die after mkdir (F36, F38).
guidance_note: Take a lock atomically before the first shared write and hold it to exit; a check-then-proceed probe of another process's state is not a lock.

evidence: Duplicate of F17; same checked-listing fix.
[ -e ] followed by mkdir -p is a TOCTOU; cfbb498 switches to plain mkdir as suggested, which then lost parent creation (F35).
guidance_note: When swapping mkdir -p for mkdir to gain atomicity, handle the parent chain that -p used to create.

evidence: sleep 0.5 between paste-buffer and Enter is a guess; the agent probed the TUI's '[Pasted text #N +<lines> lines]' placeholder and polls for it, which is the reviewer's poll-the-pane suggestion made concrete.
guidance_note: When a driver submits input to a TUI, poll for a rendered confirmation instead of sleeping.

evidence: cfbb498 added horizon_live_run_config_dir, which pipes through sed, and horizon_send's wc -l poll, without declaring either tool; a missing sed makes the new lock read as idle. The agent moved sed/wc/sleep into HORIZON_BASE_TOOLS.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new external tool call in lib.sh, add it to the preflight list in the same commit.

evidence: The cfbb498 lock only sees a launched session, so two drivers with different HORIZON_WORK_DIR overrides both pass and both reset the shared remote before either launches; 8e79b1b makes `tmux new-session` the atomic lock at the top of run-loop.sh.
guidance_note: When a fix claims to close a concurrency race, walk two interleaved invocations through every step from start to launch before calling it closed.

evidence: Same setup-window gap as F26, seen at horizon_bind_remote; the agent rejected a per-step re-check in favor of the held lock.

The goal_carries_expected - goal_carries_intact drift check was in the original horizon_observe, not in cfbb498 (whose lib.sh diff does not touch it); the agent confirmed against a real transcript that the Stop-hook line comes several boot entries after cwd. The has_turn gate it added caused F48 and F50.
guidance_note: When a live poll judges a still-forming record, define in the analyzer when a record counts as judgeable, and test both the forming state and the dead-after-evidence state.

evidence: The original launch killed any stale session, so a leftover session was harmless; cfbb498 removed that kill and made any live session the lock, so a finished run's session now blocks every later run. 8e79b1b's end_run kills the session on exit.
guidance_note: When an existing session becomes a lock, add the release on every exit path in the same change.

evidence: horizon_live_run_config_dir, new in cfbb498, is only called inside `[ -z "$(...)" ]`, so a failed show-environment returns empty and the lock fails open. The agent made a read failure die, and argued that an absent variable is the legitimate reserved-not-launched state under the new lock.
guidance_note: Never call a function that can die from inside `[ "$(f)" ]`; assign to a variable first so errexit sees the failure.

evidence: The original `for branch in $(gh api .../branches)` ran after the PR loop; cfbb498 fetched branches into a variable before `gh pr close --delete-branch`, so the branch loop DELETEs refs that are already gone and horizon_die fires on any leftover PR.
guidance_note: When hoisting a listing above a loop that mutates the listed resource, list after the mutation.

evidence: Same fail-open as F30, plus the undeclared sed from F25; fixed by assign-then-compare and adding sed to HORIZON_BASE_TOOLS.

Flag is a false positive for causation: the two-command trap string (capture then rm) is unchanged from the original PR, and cfbb498 only moved mktemp above it. The agent's end_run removed the temp files but kept two sequential die-capable steps, which F44 then found.
guidance_note: In an EXIT handler, run each cleanup step so a die in one cannot skip the next, and exit with the status captured on entry.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: copy-not-move and installing the trap before pin both date from the original PR. Moving projects/ instead of copying is the cleaner fix, and the agent's refusal to add a shell-side project filter (a second transcript reader) is sound.
guidance_note: When a record lives on a shared path, move it out rather than copy it, so the shared path never carries a previous owner's data.

evidence: cfbb498's plain mkdir fails with ENOENT when ~/.horizon does not exist yet, and reports 'already holds a run'. 8e79b1b returned to [ ! -e ] + mkdir -p under the new tmux lock instead of adding a dirname mkdir.

cfbb498 put the live-run die after the work-dir mkdir and before the trap, so a refused invocation leaves an empty work dir that blocks every later run. The first reply was posted to the wrong thread and then corrected; the eventual fix puts the lock first, as the reviewer asked.
guidance_note: When inserting a new die into a startup sequence, check what the preceding lines created and whether anything cleans it up on that path.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: STOP_HOOK_GOAL_RE is a context line in the f57a6f4 diff and predates cfbb498. The truncation at an embedded quote is real but dormant, since the current GOAL_PROMPT.md has no quote; anchoring on the template's closing suffix is a sound fix.
guidance_note: When a regex extracts free prose from a template, anchor on the template's fixed suffix rather than on a delimiter character the prose may contain.

evidence: Duplicate of F36 (mkdir before the live-run check leaves debris); fixed by taking the lock first.
Duplicate of F25 for sed/wc. Putting them in HORIZON_BASE_TOOLS follows that list's own rule ('what lib.sh reaches on its callers' behalf').
Flag is a false positive: the capture-then-rm trap body is from the original PR. Removing the temp files entirely (goal.md in the work dir) eliminates the leak.
Duplicate of F28; the drift check predates cfbb498.

With 5827d0c an untimed session does sort last and would displace 'session one'. But that needs the driver's own session, whose first user line holds the /goal, to have no parseable timestamp at all, which is a corrupt record that the report already exposes as started: null. Adding an mtime fallback would be a second clock.

Flag is a false positive: horizon_assert_authenticated came after horizon_bind_remote in the original PR (see the F1 hunk), so an unauthenticated driver wiped the shared remote before dying. 3e2965c moves the check to just after the lock.
guidance_note: Order a driver's preflight so every non-destructive precondition is asserted before the first destructive shared write.

evidence: F33 asked that no trap step abort another; 8e79b1b's end_run still ran horizon_release_run_lock then horizon_capture_transcripts sequentially, so a die in release skips capture. 3e2965c wraps each in a subshell and sets status=1, which keeps the failure loud.
guidance_note: When fixing 'step A's die skips step B' in a handler, make every step independent, including the ones the fix adds.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the shared $WORK/config for both pinnings was in the original PR's verify-instrument.sh, and cfbb498's diff only adds the -x check. Comparing against run1 is masked by the manifest-equality check above it, so this is latent, not live.
guidance_note: When two invocations write the same directory, compare the result against the last writer's inputs.

evidence: The inline readers of consecutive_with_commits and goal_carries_* predate cfbb498, so the flag is a false positive. The producer/consumer key coupling was untested (the reviewer's [LAW:single-enforcer] label is a stretch), and horizon_report_counts with a cross-test is a better fix than a schema doc.
guidance_note: When a shell consumer reads keys from a Python producer's JSON, put the reader in one function and test it against real producer output.

evidence: The comment said pinning never drives a terminal, but cfbb498 made pin-instrument.sh reach tmux has-session through the provision guard. 3e2965c rewrites the comment and adds horizon_need tmux to pin-instrument.sh.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new call path into a script, grep that script's comments and preflight list for claims about what it does not reach.

evidence: The has_turn gate from f57a6f4 does count sidechain assistant entries, unlike the goal collection. But the race needs a subagent turn before the main thread's first assistant entry, and the packet does not show whether that ordering can occur, since a subagent is normally spawned by a main-thread tool_use.
guidance_note: When a new predicate filters the same entry stream as an existing one, copy the existing exclusions (sidechain) or state why they differ.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the any()-vs-issues[-1] split predates f57a6f4. The two fields can contradict each other after a paraphrased re-goal, and deriving both from the last line plus a test is the right fix.
guidance_note: Derive a verdict field and its explanatory field from the same selected datum.

evidence: f57a6f4's `successors = [s ... if s['has_turn']]` permanently hides a successor that received the carry and died before turning, so a crashed handoff shows zero drift. 3e2965c judges a successor once it has a turn or a goal line.
guidance_note: When adding a 'not yet judgeable' exclusion, enumerate the states that never become judgeable (crashed, hung) and make sure they still surface.

evidence: The README described an unconditional rebuild after cfbb498 added a live-run refusal. 7beba50 deleted the guard and moved provisioning to run-loop.sh, so the README was rewritten to match that design instead of documenting the refusal.

Flag is a false positive: the 'copied to wherever runs are being kept, then removed' bullet is original README text, and 7beba50's diff shows it removed. The passive voice was ambiguous about who archives, not false.

F2's race (concurrent pins rm -rf the shared config dir) survived cfbb498 because the guard sees only launched runs. 7beba50 cuts pin-instrument.sh down to producing only pinned/ and the manifest, and provisions under the run lock, which removes the shared state rather than adding a second lock.
guidance_note: When a script both computes a per-run artifact and mutates a machine-wide singleton, split the mutation out to the owner of the lock before adding any guard.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the hand-spliced '$config_dir' '$HORIZON_WORK_DIR' trap quoting is in the original PR (F5 hunk) and was carried into end_run. A path containing a single quote breaks it; printf -v %q fixes it, and the agent probed it.
guidance_note: When baking values into a trap string, quote them with printf %q rather than literal single quotes.

evidence: horizon_release_run_lock, new in 8e79b1b, has a narrow has-session/kill-session TOCTOU. The reviewer's 'log and return 0' would hide a genuinely leaked lock; judging the postcondition (die only if the session still exists) is correct.
guidance_note: Write release functions to check the postcondition (resource gone) rather than precheck-then-act.

evidence: goal.md was introduced by the F33/F40 fix in 8e79b1b and the README section did not mention it. The transcripts/ omission predates review, so only part of the drift is fix-caused.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new run artifact, add it to the README's outputs section in the same commit.

evidence: cfbb498 added the -x check on the installed finalize-session (see its verify-instrument.sh diff) but left README's Verify section describing only the byte-for-byte diff.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a check to a verifier, update the doc section that lists what the verifier proves.

evidence: 3e2965c's run-loop.sh diff inserts horizon_assert_authenticated between the trap install and mkdir -p "$HORIZON_WORK_DIR". An auth die then runs capture against a missing work dir and prints a second, misleading die.
guidance_note: When moving a die-capable step earlier, re-check what the exit handler assumes exists at the new position.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: goal_carries_expected/intact were emitted by the original sessions.py (f57a6f4 changes an existing goal_carries_expected line), and the README paragraph omitted them from the start.
guidance_note: When documenting a report format, list the fields the driver acts on, not just the per-record ones.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the 'runs at this work dir' log line is original login.sh text that cfbb498's login.sh diff did not touch. It names the wrong directory.

login.sh writes the same singleton config dir without the lock the F2-cluster fix applied elsewhere. Impact is limited because login.sh returns early when already logged in, but taking the one run lock is the consistent fix.
guidance_note: When introducing a lock for a shared resource, grep every script that writes that resource and route each one through the lock.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the json.loads try/except followed by entry.get is original read_session code. A non-object JSON line raises AttributeError, and the transcript_entries generator that yields only dicts parses at the boundary rather than guarding inline.
guidance_note: When parsing line-delimited JSON, check the parsed value's type in the same unit that catches the parse error.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: project_dir="$seed_out_dir/$(basename "$seed_dir")" appears unchanged in every earlier hunk. Reading project.name from seed-manifest.json is right, and folding four manifest readers into horizon_manifest_field addresses the real duplication.
guidance_note: When a downstream script needs a value an upstream script already records in a manifest, read the manifest instead of re-deriving it.

narrative: A large horizon instrument PR went through five review rounds plus a cap-hit sixth. Round 0 found real bugs, including the memento-sha-as-goal-ref S5 reported four times. The cfbb498 concurrency fix, which used the live session as the lock and only detected launched runs, is the single largest cost: it directly produced about a dozen round-1 and round-3 findings (setup-window races, a fail-open lock read, undeclared sed, leftover empty work dirs, the missing teardown, the pin-pin race, and the login.sh gap). Smaller chains came from hoisting the branch listing above the PR-closing loop, plain mkdir losing parent creation, the has_turn gate, and moving the auth check between trap install and mkdir. Every later round also carried findings on pre-existing code because round 0's time budget cut convergence short, so no round was wholly avoidable, but most of each round's volume was fix-caused.
guidance_observations: The concurrency fix was planned in one reply covering four threads without walking two interleaved invocations through startup; that walk would have exposed the setup window, the empty-dir debris, and the pin-pin race before review did.

Fixes that added tool calls or new artifacts repeatedly skipped the matching preflight list and README update (sed/wc, goal.md, the -x check, the provision refusal), which cost a doc-drift finding per instance.

The agent's pushbacks (F10, F42) and different fixes (F30, F44, F53, F55, F62, F63) were consistently well-judged and kept loud failures loud. The cost came from incomplete fixes, not from bad accept/reject choices.
